claim_reviews.conclusion: “Shopping voucher” correctly denotes a coupon, credit, or redeemable document used for shopping.
claim_reviews.subject: English cue and sense

claim_reviews.conclusion: “Voucher belanja” is natural and widely used Indonesian retail wording.
claim_reviews.subject: Indonesian answer

claim_reviews.conclusion: “Baucar beli-belah” is valid Malaysian Malay and matches the intended sense; “baucar” is the localized equivalent of “voucher.”
claim_reviews.subject: Malaysian answer

claim_reviews.conclusion: “Different-common-word” is acceptable only as a preferred/localized-form contrast, not as an exclusive usage contrast, because Malaysian Malay also uses “voucher.”
claim_reviews.subject: Final relation

claim_reviews.conclusion: No false-friend distinction is involved; the forms are semantically aligned.
claim_reviews.evidence_limitation: The reviewed sources establish the meanings and usage equivalence but do not explicitly classify this pair as a false-friend case.
claim_reviews.subject: False-friend contrast

response.rationale: Both translations and the English sense are valid. However, the relation label can overstate the contrast: Malaysian Malay also uses voucher, while baucar is the localized/preferred equivalent. No false-friend contrast is present.
